idiom_name: module-scope cell with ??= (or a memoised promise for async init)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has one thread of control per realm, so the synchronisation half of the pattern does not exist: a module body is evaluated exactly once (ES module evaluation, and the CommonJS cache guarantees the same), which makes a module-scope binding the natural once-cell, and for genuine laziness `cell ??= build()` (ES2021) replaces the outer check with a nullish test. For asynchronous initialisation the cell must hold the promise rather than the value: `pending ??= load()` memoises the in-flight operation so every concurrent caller awaits the same work, which is the JavaScript equivalent of taking the slow-path lock. The classic check-plus-lock structure remains justified only around real shared memory - a SharedArrayBuffer with Atomics.load/Atomics.compareExchange - and even there a lock-free compare-and-swap loop is preferred over a lock.
pitfalls: `x ??= await build()` yields between the test and the assignment, so concurrent callers each start their own build - cache the promise instead of the awaited value.
??= treats only null and undefined as unset: an initialiser that legitimately returns undefined runs on every access, so use a separate flag when undefined is a valid value.
'Once per process' is false on the server: every worker thread, per-request module instance and hot-reload generation gets its own module state, so the cell is per realm, not global.
A cached rejected promise is permanent: the failure is re-thrown for every caller until the cell is explicitly cleared.
